Build a singly linked list that is last in, first out: count it, push and pop values, peek at the head, list its values and reverse it.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/simple-linked-list) (MIT). Listed under [Collections & Algorithms](/examples/?subject=collections-and-algorithms).

```nomi-run
// FILE: simple_linked_list.nomi
//# A singly linked list, used as a stack.

/// A singly linked list that is last in, first out: `push` puts a value at
/// the head, and `pop` and `peek` read the head. It is a value, so every
/// operation answers a list and shares the nodes it did not change.
pub enum LinkedList<T> {
    Empty
    Node {value: T, next: LinkedList<T>}
}

/// Why a value cannot be read.
pub enum Error {
    EmptyList
}

impl LinkedList<T> {
    /// The list that pushing `values` one after another onto an empty list
    /// builds, so the last of them is at the head.
    pub fn from(values: List<T>) -> LinkedList<T> {
        Iter.reduce(values, LinkedList.push, from: LinkedList.Empty)
    }

    /// `list` with `value` at its head.
    pub fn push(list: LinkedList<T>, value: T) -> LinkedList<T> {
        #.Node{value, next: list}
    }

    /// The value at the head of `list` and the list after it, or
    /// `EmptyList`.
    pub fn pop(list: LinkedList<T>) -> Result<#(T, LinkedList<T>), Error> {
        case list {
            .Empty -> Err(.EmptyList)
            #.Node{value, next} -> Ok(#(value, next))
        }
    }

    /// The value at the head of `list`, or `EmptyList`.
    pub fn peek(list: LinkedList<T>) -> Result<T, Error> {
        case list {
            .Empty -> Err(.EmptyList)
            #.Node{value} -> Ok(value)
        }
    }

    /// `list` with its values in the opposite order.
    pub fn reverse(list: LinkedList<T>) -> LinkedList<T> {
        Iter.reduce(list, LinkedList.push, from: LinkedList.Empty)
    }
}

impl Iter<T> for LinkedList<T> {
    /// Walks the list from its head, so `Iter.to_list` answers the values in
    /// the order `pop` would.
    fn each_while(list: LinkedList<T>, yield: (T) -> Bool) -> Bool {
        case list {
            .Empty -> True
            #.Node{value, next} -> yield(value) and each_while(next, yield)
        }
    }
}

// FILE: simple_linked_list_test.nomi
import simple_linked_list.LinkedList

/// One canonical operation and what it should answer: a count, a pop or a
/// peek of a given value or one that fails, a push, the values as a list, a
/// reverse.
enum Step {
    Count Int
    Pop Int
    PopFails
    Push Int
    Peek Int
    PeekFails
    ToList List<Int>
    Reverse
}

derive Equatable for Step

/// Runs each step's operation on the list built from `values`, in turn, and
/// answers the steps as they happened. A list that does what every step
/// says answers the steps it was given.
fn replay(values: List<Int>, steps: List<Step>) -> List<Step> {
    #(happened, _list) =
        steps
        |> Iter.map_reduce(fn list = LinkedList.from(values), step -> {
            case step {
                .Count(_) ->
                    #(Step.Count(Iter.count(list)), list)

                .Pop(_) or .PopFails -> {
                    case LinkedList.pop(list) {
                        Ok(#(value, rest)) -> #(Step.Pop(value), rest)
                        Err(_) -> #(Step.PopFails, list)
                    }
                }

                .Push(value) ->
                    #(Step.Push(value), LinkedList.push(list, value))

                .Peek(_) or .PeekFails -> {
                    case LinkedList.peek(list) {
                        Ok(value) -> #(Step.Peek(value), list)
                        Err(_) -> #(Step.PeekFails, list)
                    }
                }

                .ToList(_) ->
                    #(Step.ToList(Iter.to_list(list)), list)

                .Reverse ->
                    #(Step.Reverse, LinkedList.reverse(list))
            }
        })

    happened
}

test "count" {
    cases = [
        #("Empty list has length of zero", [], [Step.Count(0)]),
        #("Singleton list has length of one", [1], [.Count(1)]),
        #("Non-empty list has correct length", [1, 2, 3], [.Count(3)]),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, values, steps), description {
        assert replay(values, steps) == steps
    }
}

test "pop" {
    cases = [
        #("Pop from empty list is an error", [], [Step.PopFails]),
        #("Can pop from singleton list", [1], [.Pop(1)]),
        #("Can pop from non-empty list", [1, 2], [.Pop(2)]),
        #("Can pop multiple items", [1, 2], [.Pop(2), .Pop(1)]),
        #("Pop updates the count", [1, 2], [.Count(2), .Pop(2), .Count(1), .Pop(1), .Count(0)]),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, values, steps), description {
        assert replay(values, steps) == steps
    }
}

test "push" {
    cases = [
        #("Can push to an empty list", [], [Step.Push(1)]),
        #("Can push to a non-empty list", [1, 2], [.Push(3)]),
        #("Push updates count", [1, 2], [.Push(3), .Count(3)]),
        #(
            "Push and pop",
            [],
            [.Push(1), .Push(2), .Pop(2), .Push(3), .Count(2), .Pop(3), .Pop(1), .Count(0)],
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, values, steps), description {
        assert replay(values, steps) == steps
    }
}

test "peek" {
    cases = [
        #("Peek on empty list is an error", [], [Step.PeekFails]),
        #("Can peek on singleton list", [1], [.Peek(1)]),
        #("Can peek on non-empty list", [1, 2], [.Peek(2)]),
        #("Peek does not change the count", [1, 2], [.Peek(2), .Count(2)]),
        #(
            "Can peek after a pop and push",
            [],
            [.Push(1), .Push(2), .Peek(2), .Pop(2), .Peek(1), .Push(3), .Peek(3)],
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, values, steps), description {
        assert replay(values, steps) == steps
    }
}

test "toList LIFO" {
    cases = [
        #("Empty linked list to list is empty", [], [Step.ToList([])]),
        #("To list with multiple values", [1, 2, 3], [.ToList([3, 2, 1])]),
        #(
            "To list after a pop",
            [],
            [.Push(1), .Push(2), .Push(3), .Pop(3), .Push(4), .ToList([4, 2, 1])],
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, values, steps), description {
        assert replay(values, steps) == steps
    }
}

test "reverse" {
    cases = [
        #("Reversed empty list has same values", [], [Step.Reverse, .ToList([])]),
        #("Reversed singleton list is same list", [1], [.Reverse, .ToList([1])]),
        #(
            "Reversed non-empty list is reversed",
            [1, 2, 3],
            [.Reverse, .Count(3), .Pop(1), .Pop(2), .Pop(3)],
        ),
        #("Double reverse", [1, 2, 3], [.Reverse, .Reverse, .Pop(3), .Pop(2), .Pop(1)]),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, values, steps), description {
        assert replay(values, steps) == steps
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- `LinkedList<T>` is a generic enum, `Empty` or a `Node` with a `value` and the `next` list. Nomi values cannot change, so it is a persistent list: `push` answers a new head over the old list, `pop` answers the head's value and the list after it, and every list shares the nodes below its head with the list it came from.
- `pop` and `peek` answer `Result`, with `Error.EmptyList` for an empty list, the canonical "list is empty" error.
- `impl Iter<T> for LinkedList<T>` walks the list from the head, so counting and listing the values are std's `Iter.count` and `Iter.to_list`, called on the list from the tests, and `reverse` is `Iter.reduce(list, LinkedList.push, from: LinkedList.Empty)`. `Iter.count` walks the list each time, as a singly linked list without a stored length does.
- The canonical data has two mutually exclusive groups for the list's values, last in first out (`[3, 2, 1]` for a list built from `[1, 2, 3]`) and first in first out. This port takes the first, which is the order `pop` answers and `Iter` walks, and leaves out the three first-in-first-out cases.
- The canonical cases are lists of operations, so the test file follows circular-buffer: each is a list of `Step`s (`Count(2)`, `Pop(2)`, `PopFails`, `Push(3)`, `Peek(1)`, `PeekFails`, `ToList([3, 2, 1])`, `Reverse`), `replay` runs them on the list built from the case's initial values with one `Iter.map_reduce`, and each row asserts `replay(values, steps) == steps`.
- Each canonical group is a test holding one `subtests` table. Two cases that newer ones reimplement are left out: the first "Can push to an empty list", which the canonical data writes with no initial values at all, and the first "Reversed non-empty list is reversed", which the newer one extends with a count.
